title: NIST CFReDS Hacking Case: all 31 official questions
instructions: Answer all 31 official questions using only supplied evidence and the public case context. Do not read private references, published answers, saved scores or other systems' answers.
Return {schema_version:2, case_id, answers:[{question_id,status,answer}]}. Status is answered, unknown or unanswered. False and zero are claims, not synonyms for unknown.
Public schemas define typed answer roles. Required fields describe a complete response; omit unsupported fields and explain limitations outside answer. Never guess to fill a field.

Keep supporting observations, evidence paths, tools, reasoning, and qualifications in top-level submission appendices or the report, outside answer. Extras inside answer are extra assertions under the deterministic rubric.

Lists are unordered multisets. Preserve distinct observations and meaningful duplicates. Submit only requested items; do not pad with alternatives. An unresolved reference is reported separately, not silently counted wrong.

String matching ignores case and repeated whitespace only unless a question publishes another rule. Preserve filenames, full paths, account identities and unusual characters. Use single Windows path separators; do not invent a drive prefix.

Timestamps require an explicit source-supported UTC offset. Do not infer local display timezone from this profile or shift timestamps to match another source. Printed precision and event meaning must remain explicit in the evidence appendix.
An answer score is deterministic agreement with a versioned reference. It is separate from proof verification, extraction completeness, attribution, and investigation completeness.
The public source obscures a suspect name with equals signs to avoid indexing; the official scenario says those signs do not occur in the evidence. The wording is preserved in the prompts.

Where a public list_rules subset count is declared, submit exactly that many distinct supported examples. The accepted pool is private; extra or repeated submissions are not a shortcut to full credit.

For Q3 and Q8, this contract interprets the published local-time display in the contemporaneous time zone addressed by Q4. Submit a source-supported explicit offset; the public profile does not disclose that offset. This is a declared comparison convention, not proof of the original display configuration.

For Q31, report the antivirus result as a Boolean and document the actual scanner, version/signature date, scope, detections and failures outside answer. Boolean agreement does not verify that the examination occurred or that every infection was found.

Every scored answer leaf declares x-claim-requirement. This checks compatibility with specific reviewed claim roles, not English entailment or answer completeness. A currently unsupported stronger role remains unsupported; do not replace it with a generic string-valued observation.
HELD PUBLIC REVIEW DRAFT: model_run_ready is false. Do not launch model experiments or scoring from this contract.

x-claim-row same_claim_part requires all retained fields of that object to originate in the same candidate and flattened claim part. It does not itself enforce case/exhibit membership, personal identity, cross-question linkage or list completeness.

Selected-case exhibit/source membership must be enforced at runtime before any model run. Exact recorded host/configuration and scoped inventory roles below remain narrow interpretations, not proof of actual use or global completeness. Unsupported stronger meanings remain empty.

Every supporting source record must match the declared exact exhibit, source snapshot and artifact variant. Antivirus observations additionally require the declared scan-input origin. No origin may be inferred from answer text, target paths or investigator annotations.

questions.prompt: What is the image hash? Does the acquisition and verification hash match?

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Algorithm of a reviewed logical/acquisition image-digest role; a comparison result requires the separate equality relation.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: A fixed reviewed image-digest role or a same-algorithm digest comparison over the bound logical-image subject. Keep algorithm/digest source association explicit. Exact source-origin and row checks enforce the selected case evidence. Missing stronger meanings and evidence still keep this draft held; catalog compatibility is not actual-case availability.

digest.description: Hexadecimal digest of the reconstructed acquired media, not the compressed container or an individual segment.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Digest recomputed over logical media bytes, not container or segment bytes.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: A completed logical-media hash calculation tied to the examined image subject. A retained acquisition checksum is not required merely to report a computed digest; it is required for the separate comparison assertion. Exact source-origin and row checks enforce the selected case evidence. Missing stronger meanings and evidence still keep this draft held; catalog compatibility is not actual-case availability.

acquisition_verification_match.description: Agreement of acquisition and verification media digests; identify their observations separately in the evidence appendix.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Equality of acquisition and recomputed logical-image digests for the same algorithm and subject; not original authenticity.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Both bound digests and the approved equality relation. Exact source-origin and row checks enforce the selected case evidence. Missing stronger meanings and evidence still keep this draft held; catalog compatibility is not actual-case availability.

It does not establish the last successful logon or the identity of the user who performed it; a caveat in an appendix cannot enforce that distinction. Require source-supported successful-logon identity and a reviewed last-event ordering/coverage rule tied to the selected case source.

questions.prompt: This IRC program has the capability to log chat sessions. List 3 IRC channels that the user of this computer accessed.

items.description: Use recorded channel-log basenames, including their network and .log suffix, as this reference contract’s channel identifiers. Put separately recovered channel sigils/names and evidence paths outside answer; do not invent them from a filename.

questions.prompt: Ethereal, a popular “sniffing” program that can be used to intercept wired and wireless internet packets was also found to be installed. When TCP packets are collected and re-assembled, the default save directory is that users \My Documents directory. What is the name of the file that contains the intercepted data?

file_name.description: Filename of the captured/intercepted data; provide the evidence path separately.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Q23 requested answer value /properties/file_name under the full public prompt and schema description.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: traffic.file_name establishes the basename of a decoded classic-PCAP source. It does not bind that source to the referenced Ethereal capture/user directory or interception scenario. Need a source-affiliation rule rather than assuming every traffic artifact is the requested file. Exact source-origin and row checks enforce the selected case evidence. Missing stronger meanings and evidence still keep this draft held; catalog compatibility is not actual-case availability.

questions.prompt: Yahoo mail, a popular web based email service, saves copies of the email under what file name?

file_name.description: Cached filename or documented filename pattern; preserve the distinction in the evidence appendix.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Retained IE cache filename linked to a validated Yahoo Mail message URL and matching message HTML.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Use only browser.yahoo_mail_cache_file_name. The allocated index.dat record must link the retained cache filename to a validated Yahoo Mail message URL, with matching message headers/body in the examined cache content. Generic browser.cache_file_name, a Yahoo hostname alone or a guessed filename pattern is insufficient. This does not establish authenticity, ownership or user activity. All backing records retain the declared exact evidence source scope; tuple values retain their own role and native type.

questions.prompt: How many executable files are in the recycle bin?

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Count of the executable population requested by the original public question.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Independent review must establish that the declared extracted set is equivalent to the original requested executable population, including executable membership, aliases, unreadable entries, reparse handling and traversal limits. The current exact-set aggregate proves only its declared population; matching a count or linking the same claim part does not establish population equivalence. No expected-count-driven exclusions or reader changes are permitted.

questions.prompt: Are these files really deleted?

deleted_from_file_system.description: Whether filesystem metadata marks the referenced recycle-bin entries deleted; not recoverability, secure erasure or a claim that no copy exists.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Filesystem deletion state of the same executable population requested by Q28.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Independent review must establish that the declared extracted set is equivalent to the original requested executable population, including executable membership, aliases, unreadable entries, reparse handling and traversal limits. The current exact-set aggregate proves only its declared population; matching a count or linking the same claim part does not establish population equivalence. No expected-count-driven exclusions or reader changes are permitted.

questions.prompt: How many files are actually reported to be deleted by the file system?

deleted_file_count.description: Files reported deleted by filesystem metadata; do not substitute recycle-bin membership.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: reader-reported deleted-entry count in its stated filesystem scope
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Source observations must carry this exact reviewed role, native value type and bound source subject/exhibit. Question relevance and evidence scope remain separately inspectable; a differently typed fact or arbitrary annotation cannot supply this field. Exact source-origin and row checks enforce the selected case evidence. Missing stronger meanings and evidence still keep this draft held; catalog compatibility is not actual-case availability.

questions.prompt: Perform a Anti-Virus check. Are there any viruses on the computer?

viruses_found.description: Result of the declared antivirus examination; absence requires stated tool, signatures, coverage and failures.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Result of the declared scanner examination: true records at least one signature match (possibly with incomplete scope); false requires completed declared scope. Matches may be false positives; neither value establishes global virus absence, historical infection or actual malware execution.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Use the exact scanner.detections_found Boolean for the declared source examination. TRUE requires at least one recorded signature match and can coexist with incomplete scan scope. FALSE requires completion of the declared scope according to the reader. Before launch, bind scanner tool/version/signatures, source receipt, examined input and exclusions, completion/failures and selected-case exhibit scope; current leaf/row compatibility does not enforce these source/scope constraints. This is the public schema narrow scanner-result interpretation, not a global virus-presence claim.
